Skipped once signed or closed. config {reason});THAT FilterGroup IS THE FULL SAVED-FILTER VOCABULARY FOR THE DOMAIN, not an automation-only subset. For CONTACT, PROPERTY and DEAL that vocabulary is enumerable: listFilterFieldNames returns it complete, and any field it lists a conditional can evaluate. NEVER tell a user an automation cannot consider some attribute without reading that list for the workflow DOMAIN first — "it cannot see it" is usually a domain mismatch (last sold date, year built, estimated value are PROPERTY fields, not contact fields). APPOINTMENT conditionals take their own full filter group, but listFilterFieldNames and listFilterFields do not accept APPOINTMENT. That is a gap in DISCOVERY, never evidence about the capability: copy a conditional already in the graph; if you cannot confirm a field, say so rather than that it cannot be done. AI CONDITION CONTEXT — an "ai_conditional" step's `context` is a Context Layer SELECTION, not a list of ids: an object keyed by any of contact | deal | property | appointment | organization, each mapping to that source's slice flags (e.g. {contact:{includeTextMessages:true, includeNotes:false}}). A key's PRESENCE includes it; {} means that source with its defaults. Only sources the RUN carries an id for resolve (a CONTACT run has a contact), so one the domain never carries renders nothing. The step is available on APPOINTMENT graphs although "conditional" is not. A sixth key `event` is EVENT-only, and on an EVENT graph the ONE source that renders (an EVENT run carries no record): {mode:"whole"} sends the whole webhook body, {mode:"fields",paths:["call.outcome"]} only the named accessor paths (1-25, none reading the whole payload; use whole for that). `{event:{}}` is refused, and `event` on any other domain is a publish error. EVENT MAPPINGS — two rules mapping rows are REJECTED for. (1) EXACTLY ONE destination and EXACTLY ONE value source per row: a customFieldMappings row names either a customFieldId or an attributionKey (one of the org's reserved, listing-hidden attribution fields: utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content, gclid, fbclid, msclkid, ttclid, li_fat_id, landingUrl, referrerUrl), and either an accessor or a literalValue. A row naming two of either is dropped and counted at execution, never resolved by precedence. (2) A tagMappings row resolves its value to a tag or list BY NAME and CREATES one when the org has none, bounded at 25 distinct values per row and refusing values that are obviously not category names (a uuid, an email, a url, a long-digit platform id, over 80 characters); tags and lists share one org-wide namespace, so a name a list holds cannot become a tag and that row is dropped. Both counts ride the run's FIND_CREATE_CONTACT_RESOLVED audit event as tagsWritten/tagsDropped. MERGE FIELDS — the COMPLETE per-domain vocabulary a body may draw on. Substituted at run time: textBody, textBodies, emailBody, emailSubject, a Slack block's text and a Slack button's url, plus a deal node's title and a task node's name and description. NOT substituted, so braces there are left alone: a generative node's systemPrompt (an instruction to a model, not a template) and a deal node's description. Keys are matched EXACTLY, case-sensitively. There is NO dotted record namespace: {{contact.address1}}, {{contact.firstName}} and {{deal.title}} are not merge fields (the SLACK keys below are literal dotted names, not a namespace you may extend). Do not infer a key from another domain's spelling either — the shapes differ (CONTACT has contactPropertyAddress, PROPERTY has full_address); use a key off this list or none. An unknown token is NOT a missing variable and does NOT render blank: braces reach the reader verbatim (except a notify step on OMIT_BLANKS, which blanks them). promoteWorkflowDraft REFUSES a draft carrying one in a SCANNED FIELD — textBody, textBodies, emailBody (including one stored as emailBodyFormat "TIPTAP_JSON", whose merge fields are document pills rather than braces and are read as such), the WORKFLOW-LEVEL email subject on communicationConfig and a NODE'S OWN one, a fallbackTextBody under SEND_FALLBACK, an email step's fallbackEmailSubject and fallbackEmailBody, under SEND_FALLBACK and only where a PRIMARY can miss a variable (the EFFECTIVE subject — the workflow's unless sendInSameThread is false — or a body the graph carries), a Slack block's text or its button url, a deal node's title and fallbackDealTitle on a CONTACT or DEAL graph, and an inline task node's name and description — and updateWorkflowGraph returns that same judgement as workflowGroup.draftValidation on every write — a reading of the GROUP'S DRAFT, which is the version you just wrote whenever you followed the normal path and edited the draft. Edit a PAUSED version instead and the field still answers about the draft, so it is null when there is none and about a DIFFERENT version when there is: it is not a verdict on your write in that case, and nothing in the response says so ({isValid, errors}, each unrenderable token named with the field it sits in and the supported key it most likely meant). READ IT on the response to the write and fix what it names, rather than discovering it when activation fails. THAT LIST OF SCANNED FIELDS IS CLOSED, and it is still SHORTER than the list of fields that are substituted. Anything substituted at run time but absent from it is checked by nothing, so a clean draftValidation is not evidence about it — check those against the vocabulary below yourself. What remains unscanned, and NOT an exhaustive list: a PROPERTY create-contact step's deal title and fallback title (substituted against the NEW CONTACT and the workflow user, not against the PROPERTY graph's own vocabulary, so the gate has no single vocabulary to judge them by and deliberately does not try); a Slack reply node's message; and any body that lives in a referenced templateId rather than in the graph — the graph then carries no body for the scan to look at. In every one of them a wrong key promotes clean. What the recipient sees differs by path: most render through the token renderer and arrive as LITERAL BRACES, but a Slack reply node's message is interpolated by its own function, which replaces any {{slack.<field>}} it does not recognise with an EMPTY STRING — so a typo there shows as missing text, not a broken template. PROPERTY: {{line1}}, {{line2}}, {{propertyCity}}, {{state}}, {{zip}}, {{full_address}}, {{property_url}}, {{beds}}, {{baths}}, {{sqft}}. CONTACT: {{fullName}}, {{firstName}}, {{lastName}}, {{contactUrl}}, {{contactPhoneNumber}}, {{contactEmail}}, {{contactPropertyAddress}}, {{contactPropertyStreet}}, {{contactPropertyFullAddress}}, {{contactPropertyCity}}, {{contactPropertyZipcode}}, {{contactPropertyAuctionDate}}, {{contactPropertyForeclosureStage}}, {{contactPropertyAmountOwed}}, {{userFullName}}, {{userFirstName}}, {{userLastName}}, {{userPhoneNumber}}, {{userEmail}}, {{userOrganizationName}}. DEAL: {{dealTitle}}, {{dealUrl}}, {{dealPipelineName}}, {{dealStageName}}, {{dealPrice}}, {{dealCloseDate}}, {{dealPropertyLine1}}, {{dealPropertyLine2}}, {{dealPropertyCity}}, {{dealPropertyState}}, {{dealPropertyZip}}, {{dealPropertyFullAddress}}, {{dealPropertyCounty}}, {{dealPropertyApn}}, {{dealPropertyLegalDescription}}, {{dealContactFullName}}, {{dealContactFirstName}}, {{dealContactLastName}}. APPOINTMENT: {{appointmentStartTime}}, {{appointmentEndTime}}, {{appointmentMeetingLink}}, {{appointmentLocation}}, {{appointmentDurationMinutes}}, every CONTACT key above. EVENT: no merge fields at all — a {{...}} in an EVENT body is an ACCESSOR PATH into the inbound webhook payload (see the EVENT actions above), not a merge field, and is never validated against this vocabulary. SLACK: {{slack.text}}, {{slack.userName}}, {{slack.channelName}}, {{slack.permalink}}. CONTRACT: {{contractName}}, {{contractSigningLink}}, {{contractUrl}}, {{contractSignedPdfUrl}}, {{contractDeclineReason}}, every CONTACT key above, every DEAL key above.  Two conditional keys, and neither is legal on every graph: {{agentName}} resolves ONLY where the graph's TEXT sender is a marketing campaign, and a contact CUSTOM FIELD — addressable as {{ContactTag_<uuid>}}, where the uuid is a CUSTOM-FIELD id from listContactCustomFields and NOT a tag id from searchContactTags, however much the prefix suggests otherwise (ContactTag is the table that stores tags, lists and custom fields alike, so the GRN is named for the table rather than for the thing; a real tag id passes the shape check, is accepted by promote, and renders empty) — resolves ONLY on CONTACT and APPOINTMENT and CONTRACT graphs, the ones a send loads contact context for — and on an APPOINTMENT graph only from the TEXT REMINDER, which renders with the task, the contact and the user. An appointment Slack post loads the task alone, so every CONTACT key there, tags included, renders literally even though promote accepts it: the gate judges per DOMAIN, and this is the one place a domain is wider than one of its own nodes. Used outside its condition either one is unrenderable and blocks promote exactly like an unknown key.Triggers are managed through the `triggers` array: each entry is upserted by its id (mint a UUID to add one) and omitted entries are detached; only `config` syncs (`name` is cosmetic). Trigger config shapes: {type: "manual"}, {type: "created"}, {type: "mutation", filter: <FilterGroup>}, {type: "match", filter: <FilterGroup>}; a CONTACT match whose root AND holds one lastActivityAt or lastNoteTakenAt {comparison:"MORE_THAN", number, timeUnit} and no other relative date is the "no activity for N days" trigger: an hourly sweep enrolls each contact as it crosses N; CONTACT-only: {type: "inbound_text"|"inbound_call", twilioPhoneNumberIds: [...]}, {type: "inbound_email", connectedAccountIds?: [...]}; EVENT workflows have exactly one trigger shape, {type: "event_received"} — the workflow's minted webhook URL is the trigger. Minimal valid drip example (node/edge shape): nodes: [{id:"n1",type:"trigger",config:{}}, {id:"n2",type:"text_action",config:{mode:"single",textBody:"Hi {{firstName}}"}}, {id:"n3",type:"wait",config:{mode:"fixed",seconds:172800,interruptEnabled:false,interruptFilter:{id:"f1",operator:"AND",conditions:[],groups:[]}}}, {id:"n4",type:"end",config:{}}], edges: [{id:"e1",config:{},parentNodeId:"n1",childNodeId:"n2"}, {id:"e2",config:{},parentNodeId:"n2",childNodeId:"n3"}, {id:"e3",config:{},parentNodeId:"n3",childNodeId:"n4"}]. PROMOTE GOTCHA: promoteWorkflowDraft rejects the default UNSET sender (SenderNotChosen): set a real one (e.g. {type: "POINT_PERSON"}) first; getWorkflow.draftValidation lists every blocker. GRAPH CONFIG — `graph.config`, beside `nodes`/`edges`/`triggers`, NOT per-node. Every domain: `triggerOperator` "AND"|"OR" (several triggers: all or any); `triggerWindow`, which limits when ENROLLMENT may happen; `exclusiveEnrollment` true STOPS the record's runs in every OTHER workflow (not prior versions of this one) when it enters this one — "only one campaign at a time per lead"; inert on EVENT graphs. `activation.triggerEligibleRecordsNow` is RETIRED: parsed, read by nothing, enrolls nobody — do not write it. CONTACT graphs add `exitConditions.exitConditionTypes` — any of "any_inbound_communication", "inbound_text", "inbound_email", "contact_archived", "deals_closed", "outbound_from_human", "outbound_from_ai_employee", "outbound_from_other_workflow", "contact_signed_contract", "property_listed", "property_off_market"; there is no per-node way. The "outbound_from_*" three end the run when somebody ELSE messages the contact, never on its own workflow group's message. On APPOINTMENT omit `exitConditions`: any value, even {}, is rejected. `communicationConfig` is NOT contact-only: APPOINTMENT graphs take it too, for a reminder's quiet hours and sender. SEND WINDOW — the sending schedule is not in the graph: getWorkflow.sendWindow, set by updateWorkflowSendWindow. It and `triggerWindow` share the shape {timezone, days:[{day:"MON".."SUN", intervals:[{start:{hour,minute}, end:{hour,minute}}]}], timezoneMode?}. Each day has its OWN intervals ("weekdays 9-5, Sundays 12-4" is one window); an absent day is CLOSED, an interval never passes midnight (end after start), and an end of {hour:0,minute:0} is midnight at the END of the day. The older {daysOfWeek?, startTime?, endTime?} (same hours each listed day) is still ACCEPTED, but `days` is what is stored and read back. `hour` AND `minute` are BOTH REQUIRED on each time ({hour:9} alone is rejected). Clock times, not offsets: "weekdays 9-6" is one `days` entry per MON..FRI with {start:{hour:9,minute:0}, end:{hour:18,minute:0}}. No sending schedule falls back to MON-FRI 09:00-19:00 org time, so no weekends. `timezoneMode` is WHOSE clock the times are read on: "BUSINESS" the ORGANISATION's timezone, read live (New York when unset), and what an OMITTED `sendWindow.timezoneMode` reads as; "RECIPIENT" each recipient's zone from their phone's area code (toll-free, non-NANP numbers and EMAIL fall back to the organisation's); "CONFIGURED" the window's own `timezone`, fixed. `triggerWindow.timezoneMode` accepts only "RECIPIENT"|"CONFIGURED" ("BUSINESS" there is REJECTED by the graph parser) and is inert: its times are always read in its own `timezone`. The window is final: no quiet hours are added on top, for TEXT or EMAIL. SENDER — `communicationConfig.text.sender` / `.email.sender`, both allowed at once. A mode name alone is not a valid sender: most modes carry required fields. TEXT: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"MEETING_OWNER"} (appointment graphs) | {type:"PHONE", fromPhoneNumberId} | {type:"RANDOM_PHONE", fromPhoneNumberIds:[...]} | {type:"LOCAL_PRESENCE", scope, fallback} — LOCAL_PRESENCE picks a team number whose area code matches the recipient, and BOTH scope and fallback are required: scope is {kind:"ALL_TEAM"} | {kind:"SPECIFIC", fromPhoneNumberIds} | {kind:"EXCLUDE", excludedPhoneNumberIds}, and fallback is {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"PHONE", fromPhoneNumberId} | {type:"RANDOM_PHONE", fromPhoneNumberIds:[...]}. EMAIL: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"IDENTITY", fromEmail, fromClientId} | {type:"RANDOM_IDENTITY", identities:[...]}. UNSET is the creation default and activation is GATED on replacing it. A text_action or email_action step may carry its OWN `config.senderOverride` for that step alone (absent inherits): the same TEXT/EMAIL arms above except MEETING_OWNER and LOCAL_PRESENCE. SYSTEM CATEGORY — createWorkflow's separate `systemCategory` variable, not in the graph. All domains allow CUSTOM workflows, PROPERTY included, so `null` is right unless creating from a category's template. PROPERTY's one category, "PROPERTY_SIGNAL_SKIP_TRACE", is the skip-trace template with a daily cap; a `null` PROPERTY workflow is blank, started manually, by a property signal or by a custom data pipeline. A non-null `systemCategory` requires a `templateId` on the same create ("A system-category workflow needs a template id" does NOT mean property workflows are unsupported). NO domain offers "APPOINTMENT_REMINDER" or "INTEGRATION_LEAD_HANDLING" at create (READ-only): a reminder is createAppointmentReminder (isGlobal: true for every appointment); the second is minted on integration connect, then LOCKED against adding, deleting or rewiring a step.

## Call

```ts
const result = await client.workflows.updateWorkflowGraph({ workflowAutomationId: '<id>', workflowGraph: <SuperJSON> }, { idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID() })
// → Promise<UpdateWorkflowGraphMutation>
```

`<TypeName>` placeholders are pseudocode — the field-level shape of every input and of `UpdateWorkflowGraphMutation` is TypeScript, in `dist/generated/operationTypes.d.ts`.

## Variables

| Name | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflowAutomationId` | `ID!` | yes | — |
| `workflowGraph` | `SuperJSON!` | yes | — |
| `expectedUpdatedAt` | `DateTime` | no | — |
| `acknowledgeGraphWeakening` | `Boolean` | no | — |

## Gateway notes

- Idempotent: pass `options.idempotencyKey` (e.g. a UUID) so retries can never double-fire the side effect.
- Org-guarded: the gateway verifies the ids you pass belong to your organization before executing (403 otherwise).

## Response shape

The field tree of the exact selection set the gateway executes (leaf → `true`); the resolved `result` matches it.

```json
{
  "workflowAutomationsMutation": {
    "updateWorkflowAutomationGraph": {
      "id": true,
      "workflowGroupId": true,
      "name": true,
      "status": true,
      "stepKinds": true,
      "updatedAt": true,
      "workflowGroup": {
        "id": true,
        "status": true,
        "draftValidation": {
          "isValid": true,
          "errors": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
